scope: Site-wide technical SEO, performance and best practice for www.roscap.co.uk (25 sitemap URLs fetched; 18 Lighthouse 13.6 reports analysed; Playwright network capture of / and /contact-us on desktop and mobile; header, redirect, robots and sitemap checks). Key: tech-seo-perf.
summary: Lighthouse 13.6 (9 pages x 2 devices) puts mobile performance between 50 and 76 while desktop is 83 to 95, and the gap is explained by a few media files and site-wide script policy rather than Webflow itself. The homepage ships 9.8 to 10.3 MB because the hero is a 6.6 MB unoptimised MP4 from S3 plus a hidden duplicate 1.5 MB Webflow background video, both downloaded in full on phones; Track Record carries 6 MB of 0.5 to 1 MB PNG deal cards and, on desktop, a 6.6 MB uncompressed map SVG fetched from S3 (13.4 MB page); Insights loads 1 MB 1600 px PNG covers into 400 px cards (12.4 MB desktop). Every page, including legal pages, loads GSAP and three plugins from the site footer, Swiper loads on 5 pages, and gtag.js (194 KB) runs before any consent with no banner present, which together produce 280 to 820 ms TBT and 0.7 to 2.1 s of render-blocking time on mobile; all hero images are lazy-loaded so LCP is 4.2 to 6.5 s on mobile. The Google Ads landing page /contact-us scores 67 on mobile with a 5.9 s LCP on a 202 KB lazy-loaded decorative SVG and a Subject field typed as a telephone input. On-page SEO fundamentals are sound (canonicals, unique titles and descriptions, sitemap, redirects, 404s, HSTS), but there are no OG images anywhere, posts have no social tags, 9% of images have descriptive alt, structured data is thin, and internal linking is almost entirely nav and footer boilerplate, which is consistent with /our-services being slow to be discovered. Production code is served from a CodeSandbox sandbox on About and Insights, and HTML responses carry only HSTS among security headers. The fixes are specific Webflow actions: one compressed hero video with poster and no mobile autoplay, image re-exports through the Asset manager, GSAP and Swiper moved to page-level footers, eager-loading of hero images, a consent-gated GA4, OG defaults, alt text, extended JSON-LD and contextual links.
strengths: Canonical tags correct on all 25 pages; unique titles and meta descriptions throughout; Lighthouse SEO 100 on all 18 runs.

Clean URL handling: apex to www and trailing-slash variants return 301; uppercase and unknown paths return 404; /contact-us-success is noindexed; sitemap.xml has 25 URLs with lastmod and robots.txt points to it.
HTTPS with HSTS, HTTP/2 and brotli on HTML, CSS and JS via Cloudflare; TTFB 40 to 70 ms; CSS and JS cached for 1 year immutable.
Cumulative Layout Shift is effectively 0 (0 to 0.009) on every run; fonts are self-hosted woff2 with font-display: swap.
Desktop lab performance is already 83 to 95 on 8 of 9 pages; the problems are concentrated in a handful of media files and site-wide script loading, which makes the fixes tractable.
Article JSON-LD on every post and Organization JSON-LD on Home give a base to extend; the Webflow badge is off; lang attribute present; favicon and apple-touch-icon defined.
Every internal link on the 25 pages points to one of the 25 sitemap URLs (all returning 200); the visible navigation, mobile menu CTA and footer links resolve correctly.

findings.title: Homepage hero video: 6.6 MB unoptimised MP4 from S3 plus a hidden duplicate 1.5 MB Webflow background video, downloaded in full on desktop and mobile
findings.evidence: Playwright (desktop 1440x900 and Pixel 7 412x915): 58 requests, 10,306 KB on both; media 8,125 KB. `section.is-heroheader > .hero-bg.w-embed > video[autoplay muted loop playsinline]` has `<source src="https://roscap.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Roscap+Video++(1).mp4#t=1">`: 6,766,236 bytes, 1440x1078, 17.7 s, served by S3 over HTTP/1.1 with no Cache-Control and no poster; the browser fetched bytes 0-6766235 before any scroll on both devices. A second Webflow Background Video `.hero-bg.hide.w-background-video` is display:none (`.hide{display:none}`) yet still downloads its own 1,553,967-byte MP4 (`..._Roscap Video (1)_mp4.mp4`; a 5,329,657-byte webm variant also exists). Lighthouse: LCP element is the hero `video` on mobile (LCP 5.8 s; TTFB 433 ms, load delay 477 ms, load duration 684 ms) and desktop (2.0 s); cache-insight 'Est savings of 8,132 KiB'; total weight 9,793 KiB mobile, 9,874 KiB desktop; performance 66 mobile. Screenshots shots/tech-seo-perf/home-mobile-c1.png and home-desktop-c1.png show the panther frame as the hero.
findings.recommendation: Home page in the Designer: delete the hidden `.hero-bg.hide.w-background-video` element. Replace the S3 embed with one re-encoded loop: trim to 8 to 10 s, 1280x720, H.264 CRF 28 to 30 with `-movflags +faststart`, target under 1.5 MB (optional AV1/WebM second source), plus a poster frame as a 1280 px WebP under 60 KB, both uploaded as Webflow assets (HTTP/2, brotli, CDN cache). Embed markup: `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="poster.webp">` and inject the `<source>` with 3 lines of JS only when `matchMedia('(min-width: 768px) and (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)').matches`; on phones and for reduced-motion users the poster is the hero (set it as `.hero-bg` background-image too). Add `<link rel="preload" as="image" href="poster.webp" fetchpriority="high">` in Home page head so the poster becomes the LCP. Expected: home weight from 9.8 MB to about 2 MB on desktop and under 1.2 MB on mobile; mobile LCP target under 2.5 s; removes the S3 dependency.

findings.title: Track Record: 12 deal-card PNGs of 0.5 to 1 MB each (6 MB) and a 6.6 MB map SVG fetched from S3 on desktop (13.4 MB page)
findings.evidence: Lighthouse mobile: weight 7,001 KiB (images 6,386 KiB), image-delivery-insight 'Est savings of 6,002 KiB'. `.st-thumbnail-wrap > img.image` PNGs: mayfair.png 1,023 KB (765x594 shown at 392x380), rome.png 853 KB, manchester.png 696 KB, birminghha.png 635 KB, ssssshefield.png 624 KB, cannes.png 565 KB, dublin.png 546 KB, buckinghamshire.png 525 KB, bathuk.png 490 KB; each srcset offers only a 500w variant and the full file, so DPR 2 to 3 phones take the full PNG. Desktop: 13,390 KiB because page custom code runs `fetch("https://roscap.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mapwithireee.svg")` and inlines a 6,659,741-byte SVG (274 paths, 53 text nodes, 839,125 coordinates at 3 decimals, no raster), served uncompressed with no Cache-Control over HTTP/1.1; desktop DOM 1,306 elements vs 748 on mobile (mobile shows `img.map-mobile` mapp-p-800.png instead). Rounding coordinates to 1 decimal alone gives 4.8 MB (1.2 MB gzipped), so the geometry itself is over-detailed. Hero tr-hero.webp 127 KB is 1790x1260 for a 1335 px display. Screenshot shots/tech-seo-perf/track-record-desktop-c1.png (map) and -c2.png (deal cards).
findings.recommendation: Re-export the 12 deal images as WebP (or AVIF) at 800 px wide, quality 75, 60 to 120 KB each, and re-upload through the Asset manager so Webflow generates 500w/800w variants (or run Asset manager 'Compress' which converts to WebP/AVIF). Rebuild the footprint map from a simplified source (Natural Earth 1:110m, or Figma Flatten + Simplify) and run SVGO with floatPrecision 1, target under 300 KB; upload it as a Webflow asset (brotli, long cache) or paste it once into an Embed; load it only when `.map-wrap` enters the viewport (IntersectionObserver in the existing page footer code) and remove the S3 fetch. Expected saving about 6 MB on mobile and 12 MB on desktop.

findings.title: Insights and blog posts: 1 to 1.5 MB PNG cover images, wrong sizes attribute (desktop loads 1600 px variants into 400 px cards), two covers with no responsive variants
findings.evidence: Lighthouse Insights desktop: 12,389 KiB (images 11,793 KiB), image-delivery-insight 'Est savings of 11,046 KiB'; mobile 3,649 KiB, LCP 6.5 s, performance 62. Collection-list thumbnails carry `sizes="100vw"`, so desktop picks -p-1600 PNG variants of about 1 MB each: Financing Social Housing-p-1600.png 1,023 KB (1600x961 shown at about 400 px), Financing AI Data Centres-p-1600.png 1,013 KB, Property Portfolio Finance-p-1600.png 994 KB, Hotel Financing...png 1,048 KB, UK Buy-to-Let...png 921 KB, Development Exit Finance-p-1600.png 730 KB. `Roscap Blog.png` (1440x840, 1,554 KB) has no responsive variants (double-ID filename shows it was copied/uploaded outside the normal image field) and loads twice on Insights (site-asset URL and CMS URL) and as the hero of /blogs/how-real-estate-debt-advisory-works-in-the-uk (1,540 KiB wasted on mobile, page 2,164 KiB). blog4.avif is 2232x1256 at 796 KB with no srcset on /blogs/choosing-the-right-finance-structure... (782 KiB wasted, page 1,450 KiB, mobile performance 50). Screenshot shots/tech-seo-perf/insights-mobile-c1.png and -c2.png.
findings.recommendation: Re-export all 12 cover images as WebP at 1200x700, quality 75 (80 to 150 KB), and re-upload through the Blogs collection image field so Webflow generates variants (images added via API, CSV import or copied between collections do not get them). In the Insights collection list give the thumbnail a fixed max width (so Webflow writes a correct `sizes`) or add the custom attribute `sizes="(max-width: 767px) 100vw, 33vw"`. Keep lazy loading on cards; set the post hero image to Load: Eager (TS-05). Expected: Insights desktop from 12.4 MB to under 2 MB, mobile LCP from 6.5 s toward 3 s.

findings.title: GSAP (4 files) loads on all 25 pages from the site footer, Swiper on 5, gtag.js 194 KB in head: 424 to 478 KB of JS per page, TBT 280 to 820 ms on mobile
findings.evidence: Every HTML file, including the 6 legal pages, loads gsap.min.js (29 KB), SplitText.min.js (4 KB), TextPlugin.min.js (4 KB), ScrollTrigger.min.js (18 KB) and `gsap.registerPlugin(SplitText,TextPlugin,ScrollTrigger)` from the site-wide footer, plus Webflow's jQuery 3.5.1 (31 KB), webflow.schunk.f2efb (89 KB, 61% unused), webflow.schunk.e24cc (53 KB) and gtag.js (194 KB, 41% unused). swiper-bundle.min.js (37 KB, 61 to 86% unused) and its CSS load on /, /about-us, /insights, /partner-program, /track-record (the CSS is also a Link preload header on /). Lighthouse mobile: bootup 1.0 to 1.7 s; TBT 300 (home), 340 (about), 280 (services), 380 (track record), 350 (partner), 320 (insights), 330 (contact), 820 and 360 ms (posts). gtag.js causes 2 long tasks of 130 to 455 ms on every mobile run (340 to 700 ms CPU); webflow.schunk.e24cc (IX2) 366 to 515 ms; jQuery 110 to 346 ms. render-blocking-insight FCP savings: 740 ms (services) to 2,120 ms (debt-advisory post) on mobile, dominated by jQuery (1.0 to 1.5 s), the site CSS (0.8 to 1.2 s), Swiper CSS (0.8 to 1.1 s) and the f2efb chunk (0.67 to 1.05 s). Script bytes exceed image bytes on 3 of 9 pages (Our Services, Partner Program, Contact).
findings.recommendation: Site settings > Custom code > Footer: remove the 4 GSAP tags and the registerPlugin line. Add GSAP only in Page settings > Footer code of the pages that animate (Home counters and rates, About stats, Track Record map/cards) with only the plugins used (ScrollTrigger; drop SplitText and TextPlugin unless a page calls them) and `defer`. Load Swiper (JS and CSS) only via page-level footer on the 5 pages with a `.swiper`, and remove the Swiper CSS preload from the site head. Load gtag.js only after consent (TS-17) and then on `requestIdleCallback` or first interaction. Webflow's jQuery and chunks cannot be removed, so avoid adding jQuery-dependent custom code. Expected: 50 to 100 KB less JS on every page, roughly half the mobile TBT, FCP 0.5 to 1 s faster on mobile, legal pages lose 55 KB of GSAP they never use.

findings.title: Hero (LCP) images are lazy-loaded with no fetch priority on 7 of 9 pages; home hero text starts at opacity 0 until Webflow IX2 runs
findings.evidence: lcp-discovery-insight scores 0 on 15 of 18 runs; on 13 of them the LCP image has `loading="lazy"` and no `fetchpriority` (the other 2 are the home video, which only lacks a priority hint; the remaining 3 runs have text LCPs). 'LCP resources shouldn't use loading=lazy' and 'fetchpriority=high should be applied' fail for `img.hero-bg` on /about-us (LCP 6.3 s mobile; resource load delay 412 ms, element render delay 704 ms), /our-services (4.8 s; delay 372 ms), /track-record mobile (4.2 s; 378 ms), /partner-program (4.3 s; 474 ms), /insights (6.5 s; 501 ms + 788 ms load), /contact-us (5.9 s; 408 ms) and the blog cover on desktop. Every `` on the site has `loading="lazy"` (Webflow default left on). Home: `.heading-wrap[data-w-id] style="opacity:0"` (one of 9 IX2 initial states) hides the H1 until webflow.schunk.e24cc executes. Blog posts mobile: LCP is the H1 with element render delay 2,421 ms (choosing-the-right-finance-structure) and 1,180 ms (debt advisory) behind render-blocking CSS/JS.
findings.recommendation: In the Designer select each hero image (`.hero-bg` on About, Our Services, Track Record, Partner Program, Insights, Contact; `.bi-thumbnail` on the Blog template) > Image settings > Load: Eager, and add the custom attribute `fetchpriority` = `high`. In each page's head custom code add `<link rel="preload" as="image" imagesrcset="..." imagesizes="100vw" fetchpriority="high">` using the srcset Webflow outputs. Home: rebuild the heading reveal so the initial state is applied only when JS is present (IX2 'Page load' animation without an initial opacity 0 on the element, or add `.w-mod-js .heading-wrap{opacity:0}` in page CSS) and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`. Expected 0.4 to 0.8 s LCP improvement per page on mobile.

findings.title: Google Ads landing page: mobile performance 67, LCP 5.9 s, 435 KB of JS it does not use, a 202 KB decorative SVG as the lazy-loaded LCP element, and a Subject field typed as a telephone input
findings.evidence: Lighthouse mobile: performance 67, FCP 2.3 s, LCP 5.9 s, SI 3.7 s, TBT 330 ms, TTI 6.4 s; desktop 85 with TBT 220 ms from three long tasks (137, 122, 114 ms) in webflow.schunk.e24cc. Weight 764 KiB: scripts 435 KiB (gtag 195, Webflow 175, GSAP 55), images 211 KiB, fonts 103 KiB. LCP element `img.hero-bg.is-contact` = Vector-2.svg, a 202 KB wave pattern (1441x1260) with `loading="lazy"` (resource load delay 408 ms); the same file is served to the 412 px viewport. render-blocking-insight 1,060 ms (jQuery 1,124 ms, site CSS 805 ms). Longest critical chain 1,168 ms through 3 chained Finsweet attributes requests on jsDelivr. Playwright: 40 requests, 779 KB on both devices. Form `wf-form-Contact-Form`: `input#Subject` has `type="tel"` (verified in live HTML), which brings up the numeric keypad for the Subject on phones; redirect `/contact-us-success` (noindex) is correct. Screenshot shots/tech-seo-perf/contact-mobile-c1.png.
findings.recommendation: Before Ads go live: (1) hero image Load: Eager + `fetchpriority=high`; replace Vector-2.svg with an SVGO-optimised version (target under 25 KB) or a CSS repeating-linear-gradient pattern on `.section.is-contactus`; (2) exclude GSAP from this page (after TS-04 it will not load here) and keep Finsweet only if the form needs fs-mirrorclick, otherwise remove the module tag; (3) Form settings: change the Subject field type from Phone to Plain text; (4) add `<link rel=preload as=font>` for Boska-Medium and Switzer-Regular woff2 in the page head; (5) defer gtag until consent. Target: mobile LCP under 2.5 s, TBT under 200 ms, performance above 85.

findings.title: No Open Graph or Twitter image on any page; blog posts have no social tags at all
findings.evidence: Parsed head of all 25 pages: `og:image` and `twitter:image` absent everywhere; `og:url`, `og:site_name`, `og:locale` absent everywhere; the 13 static pages have og:title, og:description, og:type=website and twitter:card=summary_large_image (a large-image card with no image); the 12 /blogs/ posts have no og:* or twitter:* tags. LinkedIn (the only sameAs profile) and WhatsApp previews therefore render without an image.
findings.recommendation: Site settings > SEO > Open Graph: upload a default 1200x630 image (teal #043435 card, gold logo, one-line descriptor). Blogs template > Settings > Open Graph: bind title to Name, description to the summary field, image to the cover image; add `<meta property="og:url" content="https://www.roscap.co.uk/blogs/{{slug}}">` and `og:site_name` Roscap in the template head code. For About, Our Services, Track Record, Partner Program and Contact set the page hero as the OG image.

findings.title: Thin internal linking: /our-services reached only by boilerplate links and 2 home buttons, posts linked only from /insights, /about-us and /partner-program with zero body links
findings.evidence: Link graph of the 25 pages (body links, excluding nav and footer): /our-services receives body links only from Home (2 'Explore Our Services' buttons); /about-us, /partner-program and /insights receive 0; each post receives exactly 1, from /insights; posts contain no links to each other or to /our-services; /contact-us receives body links only from /our-services and /partner-program. The nav (6 links + CTA) and footer (11 links) are identical on all pages and make up 19 of the 20 to 32 internal links per page. GSC showed /our-services as 'unknown to Google' in October although it is in sitemap.xml (lastmod 2026-08-24), self-canonical, indexable (no robots directive) and linked as a plain `<a href="/our-services">` from every page, so the gap is discovery and priority, not a technical block. There is no BreadcrumbList, no related-posts module and no in-copy linking.
findings.recommendation: (1) GSC: URL Inspection on /our-services > Request indexing; confirm sitemap.xml is submitted and shows 25 discovered URLs. (2) Add section IDs on Our Services (`#development-finance`, `#bridging-finance`, `#mortgages`, `#mezzanine`, `#equity`) and link to them from: Home 'What We Do' copy and the service slider captions; About 'Founded on Discretion and Diligence' paragraph; each Track Record card (service type to anchor); each post's 'Learn more about Roscap's approach' block (service anchor + /contact-us). (3) Blog template: add a 'Related insights' collection list (3 posts, filtered by a new Topic option field) and a BreadcrumbList (TS-10). (4) Footer: add a 'Services' column with the 5 anchors. Expected: every key page gains 10 or more contextual inbound links; Insights posts stop being orphans.

findings.title: Title and heading hygiene: 'Partner program' title (15 chars) with 3 H1s, legal pages without H1, duplicate 'FAQs' H1 in two posts, H2 used for deal amounts

Privacy, Cookie, Terms, Disclaimer, Accessibility and Compliance pages have no H1 (title is an H3). /blogs/hotel-financing... and /blogs/uk-buy-to-let-mortgages... have a second H1 'FAQs' in the rich text; the blog template jumps H2 to H5 at 'Learn more about ROSCAP's approach'. Home uses 6 H2s for Track Record card labels ('Kensington, London', '£27.5m', 'Sheffield, UK', '£19.8m', 'Rome, Italy', '€4.6m'); About repeats the 'Suleman Rafiq' and 'Clemente M. Apollonj-Ghetti' H3s (desktop and mobile copies). Titles and descriptions are otherwise unique; descriptions 117 to 153 chars.

Partner Program page settings: title 'Partner Programme for Property Professionals | Roscap'; change the two lower H1s to H2 and '01'...'06' to H3 or styled text. Home deal cards: location as H3, amount as a `

` with the h2 class. About: one H3 per person; give the hidden copy a div with the heading class.

findings.title: Structured data limited to a thin Organization on Home and a 4-field Article on posts; no BreadcrumbList, FAQPage or dates/images
findings.evidence: Home JSON-LD: Organization {name, url, logo, description, sameAs: [LinkedIn]} only. Each post: Article {headline, description, url, publisher{name,url}} with no image, datePublished, dateModified, author or mainEntityOfPage. No JSON-LD on About, Our Services, Track Record, Partner Program, Insights, Contact (which has 5 FAQ accordions `.faqs-acc`) or the legal pages; no BreadcrumbList anywhere; no Instagram in sameAs although @roscap.uk is shown on Contact.
findings.recommendation: Site head code: Organization with @id, legalName 'Roscap Limited', email, PostalAddress (country GB), contactPoint and sameAs [LinkedIn, Instagram, Companies House 13536901]; keep the type as Organization (ProfessionalService at most) and avoid FinancialService, which would read as a regulated provider. Blog template head: bind CMS fields to add image, datePublished, dateModified, author (Organization), mainEntityOfPage, and a BreadcrumbList [Home > Insights > post]. Contact: FAQPage mirroring the 5 visible Q&As after the rule-1 rewrite (TS-16); value is entity clarity and AI retrieval rather than FAQ rich results, which Google now limits to authoritative government and health sites. Snippets in data section 11.

findings.title: Only 27 of 299 images (9%) carry descriptive alt text; team, deal, cover and hero images are all alt=""
findings.evidence: Across the 25 pages: 299 `` elements, 27 with descriptive alt (texts found: 'BE Logo White' on a hidden logo and 'Roscap insights' on one cover), the rest `alt=""`. Lighthouse image-alt passes because empty alt is treated as decorative, but the nav logo (`img.nav_logo alt=""`), 6 hero images, 5 team portraits (`img.team-image`), 12 deal images (`img.image`), 12 blog covers (`img.blog-thumbnail`, `img.bi-thumbnail`) and the Track Record map all convey content. Example: About shows 18 images, 1 with alt.
findings.recommendation: Asset manager: set alt text per asset (Webflow then applies it wherever the asset is placed): team 'Portrait of <name>, <role> at Roscap'; deals '<City>: <amount> <facility type> arranged by Roscap'; heroes short scene descriptions; nav logo 'Roscap'. Blogs collection: add a plain-text field 'Cover image alt' and bind it to the thumbnail alt in both the Insights list and the post template. Keep SVG icons as decorative (alt="").

findings.title: Security headers: only HSTS (no includeSubDomains or preload); no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or frame-ancestors
findings.evidence: `curl -I https://www.roscap.co.uk/`: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000 (no includeSubDomains, no preload); no Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Frame-Options or Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy on any HTML response. Lighthouse Best Practices (informative): 'No CSP found in enforcement mode', HSTS missing includeSubDomains and preload, 'No COOP header found', 'No frame control policy found', no Trusted Types.
findings.recommendation: Webflow hosting does not let you set response headers. Quick wins that work as meta tags: add `<meta name="referrer" content="strict-origin-when-cross-origin">` in the site head. If Roscap ever proxies the domain through its own Cloudflare zone, add Transform Rules for X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Permissions-Policy (camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()), a CSP in report-only mode first (Webflow IX2 and Swiper need 'unsafe-inline' styles) and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'. Otherwise document the gap; the risk for a brochure site with Webflow-hosted forms is low.

findings.title: Production JavaScript served from a CodeSandbox sandbox (jj59l3.csb.app) on About and Insights; rates feed depends on a personal GitHub Pages account
findings.evidence: `<script src="https://jj59l3.csb.app/script.js">` on /about-us and /insights: about 70 lines (stats counter via GSAP ScrollTrigger and `new Swiper('.slider-wrap .swiper')`), served with `cache-control: private, max-age=0, no-cache, no-store` and a Set-Cookie header; Lighthouse Best Practices drops to 96 on both pages for the third-party cookie inspector issue; CodeSandbox sandboxes can be paused or deleted at any time, which would break the team slider and counters. The same counter code is duplicated inline on Home. The live rates panel reads https://edusancheez2005.github.io/roscap-rates/rates.json (personal GitHub Pages) and sits on Home's longest critical chain (1,481 ms).
findings.recommendation: Paste script.js into the About and Insights page footer code (or upload it as a .js asset and reference it with `defer`) and delete the csb.app tag; remove the duplicate inline copy on Home or keep one shared asset. Move roscap-rates to a Roscap-owned GitHub organisation (or a Cloudflare Worker with a 3-hour cache) and keep a visible 'as of' date and stale fallback. Expected: Best Practices back to 100 on both pages; one fewer origin on each.

findings.title: No cache or compression on the S3-hosted video and map; Webflow image TTL is 23.5 hours
findings.evidence: S3 responses for Roscap+Video++(1).mp4 (6,766,236 B) and mapwithireee.svg (6,659,741 B): HTTP/1.1, no Cache-Control, no Content-Encoding (the SVG would gzip to 2,105,420 B). Lighthouse cache-insight on Home: 'Est savings of 8,132 KiB' (both MP4s have TTL 0). Webflow CDN: CSS and JS `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; images `max-age=84600, must-revalidate`; jsDelivr 7 days; HTML brotli via Cloudflare (51,645 B to 14,482 B), TTFB 40 to 70 ms.
findings.recommendation: Host the video poster/MP4 and the optimised map on Webflow assets (long cache, brotli for SVG). If anything must stay on S3, set object metadata `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `Content-Encoding` via CloudFront with compression enabled. The 23.5 h image TTL is a Webflow default and cannot be changed.

findings.title: Crawl controls are largely correct; staging subdomain is indexable, lang is 'en' rather than 'en-GB', root favicon.ico missing
findings.evidence: Canonical self-referencing on 25/25 pages; https://roscap.co.uk/* 301 to www; trailing-slash variants 301; uppercase paths 404 (no duplicates); random path 404; /index.html 200 with canonical to /; /404 path 200 (Webflow static 404 page); /contact-us-success noindex; /team 301 to /about-us. robots.txt = `Sitemap: https://www.roscap.co.uk/sitemap.xml`; sitemap 25 URLs with lastmod. Staging roscap-site.webflow.io returns 200 with canonical to www but no noindex meta or X-Robots-Tag. `<html lang="en">` on all pages. Icons via link tags (32x32 PNG favicon, 256x256 apple-touch-icon) but /favicon.ico and /apple-touch-icon.png at the root return 404. http:// to https redirect untestable from the sandbox; HSTS present.
findings.recommendation: Site settings > SEO: enable 'Disable Webflow subdomain indexing'. Site settings > General > Language: en-GB. Optional: add a 301 redirect `/favicon.ico` to the favicon asset URL and `/apple-touch-icon.png` to the webclip for crawlers that request the root paths. Confirm 'Force SSL' is enabled under Hosting (it appears to be).

findings.title: FAQ copy promises timescales and says Roscap funds projects
findings.evidence: `.faqs-acc-body` on /contact-us: 'For urgent acquisitions, Roscap can secure bridging loans in as little as 5–10 working days, subject to valuation and legal readiness. Development finance and commercial mortgages typically complete within 6–8 weeks, depending on lender due diligence and asset complexity.' and 'We also fund international projects through our global capital network'. Hard rule 1 flags promises of timescales and wording that implies Roscap is the lender.
findings.recommendation: Reword to indicative, lender-dependent language: 'Bridging facilities are often completed within a few weeks and development or investment loans typically take longer; timing depends on the lender, valuation and legal process.' Replace 'fund' with 'arrange funding for'. Apply the same text to any FAQPage JSON-LD (TS-10).

findings.title: GA4 loads in the head and fires collect hits on every page with no consent banner present
findings.evidence: gtag.js (G-H8HS2R6NLS) is in the head of all 25 pages with `gtag('config')` executed inline. Playwright on Home (desktop, fresh profile, no interaction): `analytics.google.com/g/collect?v=2&tid=G-H8HS2R6NLS...` (204) and `stats.g.doubleclick.net/g/collect` (204) fired on load. No consent banner markup exists in the HTML or rendered DOM (search for consent, cookie-banner, fs-cc, Cookiebot, CookieYes, Osano returned nothing). The approved in-house banner has therefore not shipped. Performance cost: 194 KB script, 41% unused, 2 long tasks of 130 to 455 ms per mobile run (TS-04).
findings.recommendation: Ship the approved in-house banner with Google Consent Mode v2: in the site head before gtag set `gtag('consent','default',{analytics_storage:'denied',ad_storage:'denied',ad_user_data:'denied',ad_personalization:'denied'})`, load gtag.js only after acceptance (store the choice in localStorage/cookie, expose a 'Cookie settings' link in the footer next to Cookie Policy), and update consent to granted on accept. Google Ads conversion tracking on /contact-us should follow the same gate.

findings.title: Fonts: no italic Boska face (italic headings are synthesised), 3 unused weights declared, no font preload
findings.evidence: site CSS declares 10 woff2 faces with font-display: swap: Boska 300/400/500/700 and Switzer 300/400/500/600/700, all font-style normal. Every italic display heading (`h1 > em`, `.text-style-italic`) therefore renders a browser-synthesised oblique rather than Boska Italic. Home loads 6 faces (131 KB); Boska-Light, Boska-Bold and Switzer-Semibold are declared but not requested. No `<link rel=preload as=font>`; CLS culprits list 'Web font' swaps on `h1 > em` (0.001 to 0.007, within budget). Lighthouse font-display-insight: no issues.
findings.recommendation: Add the Boska Italic woff2 (weights used in headings) to Site settings > Fonts so italics are real, or set `font-synthesis: none` and use the upright cut if italics are not licensed. Remove the 3 unused weights. Preload the two above-the-fold faces (Boska-Medium or Regular, Switzer-Regular) in the site head with `<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>`. Expected: faster text LCP on pages where the H1 is the LCP (blog posts, Track Record desktop), correct brand italics.

findings.title: Dead and hidden markup on Home: legacy hidden navbar with href="#" links, hidden duplicate video, hidden logo, 9 IX2 opacity:0 states
findings.evidence: Home DOM 442 elements (Lighthouse) includes `.container.is-nav > .hide.w-nav` (a second navbar, display:none at 390, 900 and 1440 px) containing `Home` and `Speak to us`; `.hero-bg.hide.w-background-video` (TS-01); `img.hide-tablet.hide[alt="BE Logo White"]`; 9 elements with `style="opacity:0"` awaiting IX2 (`.heading-wrap`, 3 `.stats-card`, `.wwa-image._2`, an `em`, 2 `.baserate-card`). The visible mobile menu CTA 'Speak with us' links correctly to /contact-us (verified by opening the menu at 390 px).
findings.recommendation: Delete the legacy navbar, the hidden background video and the hidden logo from the Home page in the Designer (Navigator > unused elements). Keep IX2 reveals but avoid initial opacity 0 on the H1 (TS-05).

findings.title: Images lack width/height attributes (nav logo flagged as unsized in every run); CLS stays within budget
findings.evidence: Lighthouse unsized-images flags `img.nav_logo` on all 18 runs plus 1 to 25 content images per page (none of the 266 `` elements has width/height). cls-culprits-insight attributes the only shifts to the nav logo/CTA ('Unsized image element') and web-font swaps; CLS is 0 to 0.009 everywhere, so no user-visible problem today.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit Width and Height in Image settings for the nav logo (112x31) and the hero images so the layout is reserved before CSS applies; keep `aspect-ratio` on card images via the class. No urgency.
